entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 2025 color global map
entries.finding: The visible-detail globe uses the OPAL team's WFC3/UVIS F467M, F547M and F657N global map; the OPAL readme declares the TIFF arbitrarily scaled and contrast enhanced, so the normal dataset does not publish those display values as literal true color.

entries.subject: Irwin et al. (2024) true-color Neptune reconstruction
entries.finding: Preparation matches the mean and channel variation of a checked equatorial OPAL sample to the unobscured central region of this true-color reconstruction distributed by the Royal Astronomical Society; the CC BY 4.0 reference is committed under source/color/.

entries.subject: OPAL FQ619N methane-band global map
entries.finding: The methane dataset uses the matching FQ619N global map, converted during preparation to fixed runtime rasters; the browser parses no FITS or TIFF.

entries.subject: OPAL F845M near-infrared global map
entries.finding: The near-infrared dataset uses the F845M global map from the same OPAL release, prepared to fixed runtime rasters.

entries.subject: OPAL coverage near Neptune's north pole
entries.finding: Measured on the pinned 2025 OPAL maps: coverage ends near 71 degrees north and thins toward it. At 619 and 845 nm the rows from 60 to 57 degrees north still hold dark swath seams (darkest pixel 0.37 to 0.77 of the row median, settling at about 0.80 from row 67), and the color map keeps near-black swath edges down to 42 degrees north (ratio 0.87 from row 98), so preparation starts the fill at 57 degrees north for the two bands and 41 degrees north for color and extends that row toward its longitudinal mean at the pole, which recovers no polar detail. An earlier recipe continued from 30 degrees north, overwriting observed cloud bands between 30 and 60 degrees north, and flipped the two narrow-band maps upside down; both are fixed.
entries.revisitWhen: An OPAL or other global release observes Neptune's high northern latitudes.

entries.subject: IAU 2015 report radii
entries.finding: The prepared scene uses the 24,764 km equatorial and 24,341 km polar radii from the IAU 2015 report values.

entries.subject: JPL Solar System Dynamics satellite tables
entries.finding: JPL discovery, mean-elements and physical-parameter tables supply the prepared 16-moon catalogue, which stays pinned source material even though the shared runtime mounts one detailed object scene and does not carry moon-dot or orbit-bank derivations in its active closure.

entries.subject: PDS Rings Node Neptune ring table
entries.finding: The PDS Rings Node table supplies the prepared ring radii, widths and normal optical depths; each ring's opacity is 1 - exp(-optical depth) and its color the neutral gray of a body without a measured color. Arago, the unnamed ring and the Adams arcs are not drawn: the table gives the first two no optical depth and the arcs no longitudes.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator configuration and I/F response
entries.finding: Two panel charts are prepared from the committed PSG configuration and raw I/F response, and the third uses the pinned photometric phase coefficients.

entries.subject: NASA Science Neptune facts snapshot
entries.finding: The panel prose and facts are prepared from the committed NASA Science Neptune facts snapshot.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hubble OPAL Minnaert coefficients of the color map per channel (F657N 0.50, F547M 0.80, F467M 0.88), the correction OPAL removed before projection, put back relative to the flood-lit disc centre.

entries.subject: Authored limb lighting: a 0.35 flood-light limb floor, an ambient term and a terminator ramp
entries.finding: Replaced by the OPAL Minnaert law of the color map.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Dated Hubble OPAL visible-color sequence (9 rotations)
entries.finding: One publisher RGB composite per included cycle, component FITS coverage, source-backed map frame and observation dates. Gray grid preserves missing coverage. Current scene lighting and rings remain a presentation, not the historical observing geometry. See the Hubble dates section of the README.

entries.subject: OPAL Cycles 22–23 dated maps
entries.finding: The TIFF and component FITS maps were acquired and inspected. Their red-channel Minnaert coefficient is 0.55 rather than the existing visible bank's 0.50; the 2015 map also starts at 180 degrees west longitude.
entries.revisitWhen: A separately prepared lighting bank for the older red-channel coefficient is in scope.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 approach frames as a color map
entries.finding: Built from 89 PDS GEOMED narrow-angle frames: detail from 15 green frames of 1989-08-20 at 48 to 59 km per pixel, color from 59 orange, green and blue frames of 17 and 18 August. Frames are placed by the limb of the flattened planet (residual median 0.45 px, largest 0.98 px), carried to one moment by cloud drift measured between frame pairs (2.67 to 2.83 degrees per hour westward from 3 N to 27 S) and the Sromovsky et al. 1993 wind fit elsewhere, and tied in mean color to the Irwin et al. 2024 reconstruction. Every longitude is seen from 34.8 N to the south pole.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 frames of 21 August 1989
entries.finding: The 98 green and clear narrow-angle frames of 1989-08-21 are 37 to 48 km per pixel, finer than the map’s 48 to 59. The planet no longer fits a frame: 50 of them show no limb and 12 an arc too short to fit, so 62 cannot be placed by the limb. The 36 that can were not enough to cover the planet.
entries.revisitWhen: Frames without a limb are placed by registering them against the map made from the frames that have one.

entries.subject: Björn Jónsson’s Voyager 2 map of Neptune
entries.finding: A finished 1,800 x 900 map made from Voyager 2 frames of 1989-08-17 and 18. Its author’s terms allow use with credit and ask that no copy be placed on another site, so it is not shipped.
